newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC says blow-out in oil well.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC says blow-out in oil well.

text.p: India's Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) said fire broke out on Wednesday in one of its oil wells in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh and the extent of damage was being assessed.
"There is a blow-out," an ONGC official in the Indian capital told Reuters. "We are still assessing the extent of damage."
"We have not received complete details," said another official.
The official said the fire broke out at 1:30 p.m. (0800 GMT) in an oil well in the Mandapetta area, about 350 km (215 miles) east of the Andhra Pradesh capital Hyderabad.
"The fire is still going on," an official at ONGC's control room set up at Rajahmundry, about 55 km (34 miles) from Mandapetta, told Reuters.
ONGC is India's largest state-run oil exploration and drilling firm.
The ONGC official at New Delhi said the fire broke out when a rig belonging to one of the contractors, Hightech, was drilling in one of ONGC's wells.
"We know Hightech had drilled up to 2,754 metres when the blow out occurred," said the official. He said the well was targeted for a depth of about 4,000 metres.
"This area is a bit complicated. This looks like a high pressure pocket," he said.
The official said the company had been doing drilling work for ONGC for the past two years and ONGC would offer all help to control the fire.
He said a senior ONGC official from New Delhi was leaving to assist authorities in controlling the fire.
United News of India said the blaze erupted during drilling, and flames leapt 55 feet (17 metres) in the air amid billowing clouds of smoke.
The news agency said police evacuated the residents of two nearby villages.
